config.prompt: Soho, 1854 — drag the investigation into order:
items: Cholera epidemics kill thousands; the dominant theory blames miasma — bad air
Snow, sceptical, maps the deaths: they cluster around the Broad Street pump
The brewery's workers, who drink beer rather than water, are nearly spared
The exception that proves the rule: a widow miles away dies of water carted from Broad Street
The handle comes off the pump; the epidemic ebbs
config.why: No germ theory to lean on — Vibrio cholerae was identified in 1883. Population data and a comparison carried the whole argument.

activities.caption: true or false — the founding case, read carefully
activities.name: epSnowJudge

statements.s: Snow's investigation proved the germ theory of disease.
statements.why: It could not have: the cholera bacterium was not identified until 1883, almost three decades after the handle came off.

statements.s: The brewery's workers were nearly spared because they drank beer, not water.
statements.why: A natural comparison group, differing from their neighbours chiefly in the exposure.

statements.s: The Hampstead widow's death was evidence against the pump hypothesis.
statements.why: It confirmed it — she drank water her son had carted from Broad Street, miles from the pump.

statements.s: A contrast between exposed and unexposed groups is still epidemiology's unit of inference.
statements.why: The art is ensuring the groups differ only in the exposure you care about.

activities.anchor: reported case counts were nearly meaningless
activities.caption: pair each measure with the question it answers
activities.name: epMeasuresMatch

config.prompt: Four measures carry the field — pair each with its question:

pairs.left: incidence — new cases per population per time
pairs.right: is this happening now, and growing?

pairs.left: prevalence — all existing cases at a moment
pairs.right: how big is the burden on services?

pairs.left: case fatality rate vs infection fatality rate
pairs.right: the denominator: deaths among diagnosed cases, or among all infected?
deaths above the seasonal baseline — needing no tests and no paperwork

config.why: Early-pandemic CFRs near 5% reflected the severely ill who got tested; the true IFR sat closer to 0.5–1% — and the difference shaped every policy argument.

activities.anchor: Always ask which question the number
activities.caption: file each scenario by which measure moves
activities.name: epPrevBuckets

config.prompt: Incidence or prevalence? File each scenario:

items.label: the early-warning jump of a growing outbreak
new cases per population per time
a chronic disease's patients surviving longer on better treatment
all existing cases at a moment
a sign of success, not failure
the metric that says an outbreak is growing

config.why: Only a rising incidence means an outbreak is growing; prevalence also accumulates when patients survive longer. The number's question is 'burden', not 'growth'.

activities.caption: call the herd threshold for a mild contagion
activities.name: epFluEstimate

config.prompt: Seasonal influenza's R₀ sits around 1.5. The herd immunity threshold is 1 − 1/R₀ — roughly what share of the population must be immune for transmission to burn out?
config.why: 1 − 1/1.5 ≈ 33% — far below measles' 92–95% for R₀ of 12–18. Compare early COVID at R₀ = 3: about 67%, unreachable early without the hard way.
config.context: That gap is why interventions aim at pushing the effective reproduction number below 1 rather than at instant herd immunity.

activities.anchor: why the peak arrives when the susceptible pool is drawn down
activities.caption: which trace is the self-limiting wave?
activities.name: epSirTrace

config.prompt: x = time, y = new infections per week — which trace is the self-limiting epidemic wave?
config.why: An epidemic consumes its own fuel: every infection converts a susceptible person into an immune one, dragging the effective reproduction number down until the wave crests — roughly symmetric, and why a prematurely relaxed population simply starts the next wave. Curve A is cumulative infections; C never self-limits.

activities.anchor: Snow's water companies were such a split
activities.caption: walk the design-selection decision
activities.name: epDesignBranch

config.root: The question decides the design; each rung buys causal strength at a cost.

start.text: A rare outbreak has just occurred and the exposure must be identified fast. Which design do you field?

choices.label: Case-control — start from outcomes, look backwards
choices.feedback: Fast and cheap — ideal for rare diseases and outbreaks.

choices.label: Cross-sectional survey — who has what now

cc.text: Compare people who got the disease with matched people who did not, and look backwards for the exposure. The signature hazard is recall bias — sick people search their memories harder.

cs.text: A snapshot of prevalence — but with no sequence, it cannot separate cause from consequence. Useful for burden, not for mechanism.

cohort.text: The cohort study runs forward: recruit thousands, record exposures, follow for years. Doll and Hill's British Doctors Study tracked 34,000 doctors and established the smoking–cancer link. Its hazard is confounding; its elegant escape is the natural experiment.

config.why: At the top, the randomised controlled trial manufactures the comparison by lottery — slow, expensive, often unethical — which is why the observational craft remains irreplaceable rather than inferior.

activities.anchor: the honest resolution is always the same ledger
activities.caption: fill Rose's ledger
activities.name: epRoseCloze

config.text: Geoffrey Rose's prevention %%0%% states that a large share of disease burden comes from the many at modest risk, so shifting the whole distribution — a little less %%1%% for everyone — prevents more strokes than perfectly treating the few. Screening inherits every %%2%% problem from the diagnosis lesson — with low prevalence, most positives are false — and adds %%3%%: finding indolent conditions that would never have harmed the patient, then treating them anyway.
config.hint: One is Rose's word, one a seasoning, one a mathematician, one the screening harm.
